summary: Connect limb and body motion to actual movement or commanded pose rather than an unrelated clock.
objective: Connect limb and body motion to actual movement or commanded pose rather than an unrelated clock.
example_prompts: Use articulation from controlled movement for the scene, preserving its model and user controls.

principles: The root controller, joint pose and secondary decoration need distinct responsibilities.
A stylized gait can exaggerate timing while preserving the intended contact and clearance story.
implementation: Choose a body plan, joint pivots and motion range before animating the whole creature.
Drive gait phase from actual progress where appropriate; handle blocked motion, stopping and turning explicitly.
Use a pose or animation tool for articulation and a controller or solver for world constraints as needed.
observable_checks: A blocked root does not continue an unqualified walking cycle indefinitely.
Turning and full limb extension remain within the chosen clearance envelope.

creative_affordances: Adapt the layout, visual treatment and timing to the task; these are reusable design proposals, not mandatory templates.
known_limits: Authored interaction/presentation guidance; no new scientific claim, accessibility certification or runtime verification is asserted.
